rationale: M19 (master review). A vocabulary DECLARATION is written on its `name=` attribute, and a formatted document routinely puts that attribute — or the value itself — on a different line from the tag that opens the declaration. Both the symbol and the `contains` edge were anchored to the ELEMENT, so a reader following either to its line landed one or two lines above the string that spells the name. Measured over the 2,500-file blast radius: 4 of 19,852 declarations, in 2 files. Small, and small is the point: every other instrument missed it, because each asks the analyzer a question it can answer correctly while the LINE is wrong, and the differential compares label+target only. The anchor is the line carrying the VALUE, which is the Attribute when the two share a line and the AttValue when the keyword and the value are split. Each entry below names a DIFFERENT shape: attribute on the next line (28, 37), keyword and value split across lines (24, 33), and a value with surrounding whitespace that is trimmed (36). A fixture that only covered the first shape would pass against a fix that got the other two wrong. The complexType is named distinctly from the element that uses it, because a fixture that cannot tell two same-named declarations apart would be asserting against whichever one the runner's first-match lookup happens to find — a pin that passes for the wrong reason is the failure mode the overlap-aware comment in the runner warns about.

expectRelationships.note: `<xsd:element name=` is on 23 and the value `"SplitKeywordAndValue"` is on 24, so the declaration is reported on the line the NAME is written on rather than the line the tag opens on.
the tag is on 27 and `name="AttrOnNextLine"` is on 28.
